text: There was a little girl who loved red clothes. Her grandmother (literally: "her parents' parent") was an old woman who lived far away. The old woman was ill, so the girl took her some food. On the road, a wolf (literally: "a big bad animal") came up. The wolf asked: "Where are you going?" The girl wasn't scared and said: "To my grandmother's house." The wolf ran to the grandmother's house and ate her. He put on her clothes and lay down in her bed (literally: "the sleeping place"). The girl came and said: "What big eyes you have!" (Literally: "your looking parts.") "All the better to see you with!" (Literally: "because I want to look at you well.") "What a big mouth you have!" "All the better to eat you with!" And the wolf ate the girl too. A man heard the noise, came in, and struck the wolf. The grandmother and the girl came out of the wolf, and neither of them was dead.

gaps.note: the dictionary's form of 狼 is 10 words (jiào "ào-ào"-de, bù zài jiā-lǐ huó-de dòng-wù), and in a sentence of its own its jiào reads as "is called Ao-ao"; the English gives "a big bad animal" itself, so that is used, and a reader may not see that it is a wolf

"tǎng zài lǎo nǚ-rén-de shuìjiào-de dì-fang", "... lǎo nǚ-rén shuìjiào-de dì-fang", "... tā-de shuìjiào-de dì-fang" and "zài lǎo nǚ-rén shuìjiào-de dì-fang tǎng" can't mean "he lay down in her bed" in any of the first 500 readings; the owner is left to the house the wolf is in

blind.whole: A little girl who loves red clothes goes to take food to her grandmother, an old woman who lives far away and is unwell. On the road a big bad animal asks her where she is going, and she tells it, without fear. The animal hurries to the grandmother's home, eats her, puts on her clothes and lies in her bed. When the girl comes she says how big its eyes are, and it says that is so it can see her well. Then she says how big its mouth is, and it says that is so it can eat her, and it eats her too. A man hears the noise, comes in and hits the animal. The grandmother and the girl come out of the animal's belly alive.
blind.unsure: Sentence 3: I read 'bàba-māma-de māma' as 'the mother of her father and mother', so her grandmother. Sentence 5: 'Tā shēntǐ bù hǎo' and 'tā jiā' could refer to the girl or to the old woman. Since the old woman was the subject just before, and the girl is taking food to her, I read both as the old woman. Sentence 7: the text never says what kind of animal it is, only 'a big bad animal', so I have not named it. Sentence 14: the gloss gives 'floor-side', but I read 'dì-fang' as 'place', and 'the place for sleeping' as a bed. Sentence 18: the gloss gives 'hole' for 'kǒu'. Here it means mouth. Sentence 21: the gloss gives 'difficult-human being' for 'nán-rén', which is the wrong sense. It means a man. Sentence 22: 'dǎ le' only says he hit or beat the animal. It does not say he killed it. Sentence 23: coming out 'from inside the animal' means it had swallowed them whole, but the text does not say how they got out.

notes: Translated by hand following the translate skill (2026-10-22), the whole dictionary as the level. kb_memory returned the book's own lines of this story (lesson none, mostly 100% shared); they were reused as step 2 allows and each source names its line. Changes from the book's lines: long lines split (each half kept); "Zài lù-shàng, ..." and "Yǒu yī-ge X, tā ..." read first as calling out (calling-hail), so the road is said with zài + place + zǒu and the girl gets a sentence of her own; jiù added for "so"; "chī-de dōng-xi" after ná reads as a clause (the thing someone ate), so fàn (meal); yǎnjing (eye) for the book's kàn-de bù-fen; the dialogue lines name the speaker. Not said, by choice: "some" (food), "her" (bed, see gaps), the girl calling the grandmother "my grandmother" (she says "the old woman's home"). "Neither ... dead" has no entry (kb_lookup: nothing for dead or neither) and is said by dōu méi sǐ, they all did not die. kb_gloss shows nán-rén as "difficult-human being" (nán is spelled 难) and kǒu first as "hole", which a blind reader might misread. Glossary proposal: wolf (in a story) -> dà huài dòng-wù: the test set's own literal, short, and the dictionary's form is 10 words whose jiào reads as "is called". Glossary proposal: girl -> xiǎo nǚ-rén: the book's lessons and stories say it; nǚ-hái-zi is spelled with hái (还) for its sound. Glossary proposal: grandmother -> bàba-māma-de māma: a parent's mother on either side; the dictionary's bàba-de māma (奶奶) is the father's mother only. Glossary proposal: took food to X -> ná fàn qù X jiā: with chī-de dōng-xi the meant reading is not in the first 500. Translated before kb_memory hid the stories' own lines (HAOSHUODE_MEMORY_SKIP), so some sentences reuse the book's lines and the book overlap is higher than a fresh run would give.
